BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook; Seller Update draft; Disclosure Letter SPA-003

---

## 0. Preliminary point: disregard the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's covering note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted." **We should not proceed on that basis, and we should say so in writing.**

- Nothing in our playbook or instructions records agreement to any of these positions. Several of them directly contradict our baseline. The cap, thresholds, time limits, fraud carve-out, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay are all labelled [STANDARD], and all depart materially from our positions.
- The labels are the Seller's own characterisation, inside the Seller's own draft. If we accepted them, we would be conceding almost every key economic and risk-allocation point without negotiating it.
- **Action:** Our cover email to the mark-up should state that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation. It should also state that no clause is agreed until the SPA is signed, and that the review covers the whole package. This prevents any later argument that we acquiesced.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits, whatever its label.

---

## 1. Limitations package

### 1.1 General Warranty cap (cl. 12.1): Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Departure:** Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6.0m**. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback. We may use it only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft, and **no such authority has been given**.
- **Push back:** Restore 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the team wants to trade towards it later, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority first.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl. 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess only
- **Departure:** The de minimis is 5x our position (AUD 5k). The basket is 5x our position (AUD 50k). The basket is also a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Together, these would screen out a large range of real claims and make even valid claims recoverable only above AUD 250k.
- **Push back:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller **liable from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded. Claims below de minimis should still count towards the basket. Our playbook is silent on this, but it is a standard ask and consistent with our position.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl. 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus "applies to all Claims"
- **Departure:** Our position is **24 months**. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Hidden override:** The sentence "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims into the general regime. That breaches our rule against a hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** General claims 24 months. Delete the "all Claims" sentence. Instead, add an express statement that the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, with separate regimes for each other category.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties: same cap and time limit as general warranties
- **Departure:** Fundamental and Title claims need a **separate regime**: a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify capping the Buyer's recovery on title at 20% of price. Title is the core of what we are buying.
- **Push back:** Reinstate a separate Fundamental regime on our terms.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) applying to "all Claims of any nature"
- **Departure: critical.** As drafted, the caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would apply to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Our playbook requires these to be carved out of **all** limitations to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one on our side can waive this.**
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers are excluded from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause. Separately, limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language so it does not override Title, Tax, IP, the specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Departure:** The letter deems disclosed everything in the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and deemed-search disclosure.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Only matters disclosed in the specific paragraphs, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess their nature and scope, should qualify the Warranties. Data-room documents may be referred to only as support for a specific disclosure. Disclosure should never qualify Title or Capacity warranties, or the specific indemnities.
- **Note on 1.4:** The "no admission" language is broadly acceptable. However, we should ensure it does not dilute the factual accuracy of the specific disclosures. Those disclosures are helpful to us; see section 3 below.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Departure:** This is a blanket bar on any claim about matters the Buyer or **its advisers** knew, or which were "discoverable from the data room or public records." That is broader than actual knowledge and effectively converts the data room into a complete defence. It contradicts our playbook outright.
- **Push back:** Delete cl. 8.3. If the Seller insists on some qualifier, any knowledge concept must be limited to Seller-side knowledge of **named Seller knowledge persons**, after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. We should also add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge.

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its "Key Negotiated Positions." We should use that in negotiation.

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** Bluefen represents ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%), under a change-control clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3 (DD-002). The Seller admits (DL para 2) that it has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the conditions have been satisfied.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours only, with the Condition treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." That is consent-on-delivery, which our playbook rejects. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size. Calling the matter "addressed" is not accurate given the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent that requires an **effective** Bluefen consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, **plus evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - The Condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Upgrade the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to best/all reasonable endeavours with defined steps, and add a Buyer right to review correspondence with Bluefen.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2 (DD-003). The Seller admits the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (DL para 3).
- **Departure:** The Seller proposes a "release to be provided following Completion." Our playbook requires a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. We could accept a post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the Completion funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - Require executed deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements and any other security discharges to be delivered at Completion.
  - Do not offer the post-Completion alternative.

### 3.3 Employee closing bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005)
- **Facts:** Conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller admits these are **not** in the draft funds flow, and that the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs (DL para 5).
- **Departure:** "A matter for the Seller" while omitting the bonuses from the funds flow is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer bears the cost on a debt-free basis.
- **Push back:** Either show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation as applicable) as a specific funds-flow line item and Debt-like deduction, or have the Seller fund them directly. Back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts that become payable after Completion when the continued-employment conditions are met.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- **Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Seller acknowledges this is not independent verification. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Departure:** The Seller limits the indemnity to the specific SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." This does not cover the actual risk, which is that the Company does not own, or cannot use, the SOW3 Project Materials, together with any related claims by Ironquay.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from the Company's failure to own or have unencumbered rights to the SOW3 Project Materials, and from any Ironquay claim about SOW3. Preserve the cure route: payment of the SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as established either way. Ask for evidence of payment status, such as bank records or an Ironquay statement.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external email address. Up to ~1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). The facts do not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required (DL para 6).
- **Departure:** The Seller's statement that the matter is "not expected to be material" is an unsupported conclusion. Its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary. We should not accept that characterisation, but we should not overstate the matter either. On the current record there is **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified exposure.
- **Push back:** Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve all relevant logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - make no notifications or admissions without consulting the Buyer, except as required by law.

  Exclude the incident from any general disclosure that would qualify the data-protection warranties. Consider a specific indemnity scoped to losses actually arising from the incident, with no fixed number assumed.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008, DD-011)
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each are disclosed to be read together. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course (DL para 8).
- **Departure:** The Seller asserts they are "ordinary-course operating costs." That assertion is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Approach:** Do not accept the characterisation, and do not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction. Ask for the contracts, timing, scope, termination rights and accrual treatment. Assess whether they were entered into outside the ordinary course or around the deal timeline. Then decide whether they belong in Debt, working capital, a conduct-of-business covenant or a specific warranty.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller calls these "settled under the general regime above." Under our playbook they remain **open**. Treating them as settled would also subject them to the general cap, thresholds and 18-month period, which is another hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** Record that Tax and IP terms are open and must be negotiated as separate categories. We should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution in either direction.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Departure:** The Seller relies solely on its own share register. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. The Seller itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification (DL para 10).
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances and authority. This would include an ASIC company extract consistent with the register, share certificates, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution), and confirmation of no options, rights or security over the shares. All of this sits alongside full Title and Capacity warranties under the Fundamental regime.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority
- The disclosures describe a lease notification obligation and an assignment restriction. Neither is described as requiring consent to a share sale. These are not playbook items. However, we should confirm against the underlying documents that no change-of-control trigger exists, and include the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion deliverable.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [STANDARD] labels / "already accepted" | Claims clauses are cleared | **Reject in writing**; nothing agreed until signing |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m**; no fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | General claims period | 18 months; applies to all Claims | **24 months**; delete the "all Claims" override |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **100% cap, at least 6 years**, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | Limitations apply to all Claims | **Full carve-out**; non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room, registers, public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers / discoverable | **Delete**; any qualifier = named Seller persons + reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence of cl. 11.3 conditions** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs + indemnity** |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity | **Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation and update covenants**; no assumed breach |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Investigate**; no automatic Debt or deduction |
| 14 | Tax/IP | Settled under general regime | **Open; separate categories** |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title/encumbrance/authority evidence** |

**Escalations and authority:** The Seller has opened at our fallback positions on the cap (20%) and the claims period (18 months). We must not concede either without **Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft**. The same applies to any post-Completion Riverlark release. The fraud carve-out cannot be traded by anyone. If the Seller resists it, escalate rather than compromise.

**Negotiation leverage:** Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter against its Update. The letter admits there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark repayment or discharge, bonuses missing from the funds flow, an unverified Ironquay position, a preliminary incident investigation and register-only title evidence. That record undermines the Seller's claims that these matters are "addressed," "adequate," "ordinary course" or "settled."

If the Seller insists on some qualifier, any knowledge concept must be limited to Seller-side knowledge of **named Seller knowledge persons**, after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. We should also add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its "Key Negotiated Positions." We should use that in negotiation.

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** Bluefen represents ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%), under a change-control clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3 (DD-002). The Seller admits (DL para 2) that it has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the conditions have been satisfied.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours only, with the Condition treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." That is consent-on-delivery, which our playbook rejects. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size. Calling the matter "addressed" is not accurate given the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent that requires an **effective** Bluefen consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, **plus evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - The Condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Upgrade the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to best/all reasonable endeavours with defined steps, and add a Buyer right to review correspondence with Bluefen.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2 (DD-003). The Seller admits the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (DL para 3).
- **Departure:** The Seller proposes a "release to be provided following Completion." Our playbook requires a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. We could accept a post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the Completion funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - Require executed deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements and any other security discharges to be delivered at Completion.
  - Do not offer the post-Completion alternative.

### 3.3 Employee closing bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005)
- **Facts:** Conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller admits these are **not** in the draft funds flow, and that the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs (DL para 5).
- **Departure:** "A matter for the Seller" while omitting the bonuses from the funds flow is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer bears the cost on a debt-free basis.
- **Push back:** Either show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation as applicable) as a specific funds-flow line item and Debt-like deduction, or have the Seller fund them directly. Back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts that become payable after Completion when the continued-employment conditions are met.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- **Facts:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Seller acknowledges this is not independent verification. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Departure:** The Seller limits the indemnity to the specific SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." This does not cover the actual risk, which is that the Company does not own, or cannot use, the SOW3 Project Materials, together with any related claims by Ironquay.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from the Company's failure to own or have unencumbered rights to the SOW3 Project Materials, and from any Ironquay claim about SOW3. Preserve the cure route: payment of the SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as established either way. Ask for evidence of payment status, such as bank records or an Ironquay statement.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external email address. Up to ~1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). The facts do not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required (DL para 6).
- **Departure:** The Seller's statement that the matter is "not expected to be material" is an unsupported conclusion. Its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary. We should not accept that characterisation, but we should not overstate the matter either. On the current record there is **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified exposure.
- **Push back:** Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve all relevant logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - make no notifications or admissions without consulting the Buyer, except as required by law.

  Exclude the incident from any general disclosure that would qualify the data-protection warranties. Consider a specific indemnity scoped to losses actually arising from the incident, with no fixed number assumed.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008, DD-011)
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each are disclosed to be read together. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course (DL para 8).
- **Departure:** The Seller asserts they are "ordinary-course operating costs." That assertion is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Approach:** Do not accept the characterisation, and do not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction. Ask for the contracts, timing, scope, termination rights and accrual treatment. Assess whether they were entered into outside the ordinary course or around the deal timeline. Then decide whether they belong in Debt, working capital, a conduct-of-business covenant or a specific warranty.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller calls these "settled under the general regime above." Under our playbook they remain **open**. Treating them as settled would also subject them to the general cap, thresholds and 18-month period, which is another hidden general-regime override.
- **Push back:** Record that Tax and IP terms are open and must be negotiated as separate categories. We should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution in either direction.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Departure:** The Seller relies solely on its own share register. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. The Seller itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification (DL para 10).
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances and authority. This would include an ASIC company extract consistent with the register, share certificates, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution), and confirmation of no options, rights or security over the shares. All of this sits alongside full Title and Capacity warranties under the Fundamental regime.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority
- The disclosures describe a lease notification obligation and an assignment restriction. Neither is described as requiring consent to a share sale. These are not playbook items. However, we should confirm against the underlying documents that no change-of-control trigger exists, and include the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion deliverable.

**Escalations and authority:** The Seller has opened at our fallback positions on the cap (20%) and the claims period (18 months). We must not concede either without **Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft**. The same applies to any post-Completion Riverlark release. The fraud carve-out cannot be traded by anyone. If the Seller resists it, escalate rather than compromise.

**Negotiation leverage:** Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter against its Update. The letter admits there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark repayment or discharge, bonuses missing from the funds flow, an unverified Ironquay position, a preliminary incident investigation and register-only title evidence. That record undermines the Seller's claims that these matters are "addressed," "adequate," "ordinary course" or "settled."
